name: Straight-Arm Cable Pulldown — Straight Bar
description: The straight-arm pulldown with a straight bar is performed identically to the rope version but with both hands fixed to a rigid bar, keeping the hands in a pronated position throughout. The fixed grip limits the ability to externally rotate the hands at the bottom compared to a rope, but allows for heavier loads and a more consistent pulling path. It is a reliable lat isolation finisher.

execution.starting_position: Attach a straight bar to a high-pulley cable. Stand facing the cable, hinge slightly at the hips, and grip the bar with an overhand grip, arms extended toward the cable.
execution.setup_instructions: Position body 2-3 feet from the cable stack. Slight forward lean increases lat engagement at the top.
steps: Step 1: Stand with arms extended toward the cable at approximately head height, overhand grip on bar.
Step 2: Keeping the arms straight (soft elbow), initiate the pull by contracting the lats.
Step 3: Drive the bar in a downward arc, keeping it close to the body.
Step 4: Finish with the bar pressed against the thighs and lats maximally contracted.
Step 5: Slowly return to start against cable resistance.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on pull, inhale on return.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows and converting to a pulldown
Swinging the torso to generate momentum
Not fully straightening the arms at the top
safety_considerations: Light isolation load only — do not load this movement heavily
Keep soft bend at elbow to protect the joint
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Arms extended to roughly head height at the start, bar pressed to thighs at the finish.
coaching_cues: Think: lats are pulling, not arms
Full extension at the top before every rep
